fields.Front:
[Kotlin Decision]
AI generates:
var userList = listOf("Alice", "Bob")
userList = userList + "Charlie"
Why reject this in state management? What is the correct pattern?
fields.Back:
Problem: Reallocates whole list on heap every change + var allows reassignment races.

Decision:
1. If local mutable accumulation needed: val userList = mutableListOf(...)
2. If reactive UI state: val userList = MutableStateFlow<List<String>>(...)

Rule: Always val by default. Only use var when mutation strictly required.

fields.Front:
[Kotlin Tour: Hello World]
Difference between "$user" and "${user.name}" in string templates?
fields.Back:
$user evaluates a single variable identifier directly.

${...} evaluates arbitrary expressions, property access chains, or function calls before converting result to String.

fields.Front:
[Kotlin Variables]
Does val mean the object itself is immutable?
fields.Back:
No. val is a read-only reference (cannot reassign the variable pointer).

If pointing to a mutable object (e.g. val list = mutableListOf(1, 2)), contents can still be mutated (list.add(3)).

fields.Front:
[AI Code Audit]
AI declares top-level:
var currentUser: User? = null
What risk does this create in an Android app?
fields.Back:
Risk: Global mutable state.
1. Leaks memory or persists stale state across Android Activity lifecycles.
2. Thread-unsafe: concurrent writes cause crashes or data corruption.

Fix: Scope state inside a ViewModel or inject via Dependency Injection (Hilt/Koin).

fields.Front:
[Kotlin Types]
When should you write explicit type annotations instead of relying on Kotlin type inference?
fields.Back:
1. Public API / ViewModel boundaries: Establishes clear contract.
2. Complex expressions: Prevents accidental type widening (e.g. Int vs Long).
3. Abstract types: When exposing an interface rather than implementation (e.g. val list: List<T> = mutableListOf()).

fields.Front:
[Kotlin Null Safety]
Difference between String and String? in Kotlin type system?
fields.Back:
String is guaranteed non-null at compile time. It can never hold null.

String? is nullable. The compiler strictly forces null checking before dereferencing.

fields.Front:
[AI Code Audit]
AI generates:
val name: String? = apiResponse.userName
val length = name!!.length
Why is this dangerous, and how to fix?
fields.Back:
Bug: !! (not-null assertion) throws NullPointerException at runtime if name is null.

Fix: Safe call + Elvis operator fallback:
val length = name?.length ?: 0
Rule: Treat !! as an AI red flag in production code.

fields.Front:
[Kotlin Idiom]
How does the Elvis operator (?:) behave with early returns?
fields.Back:
Right-hand side of ?: can be an expression, return, or throw:
val user = userRepository.getUser() ?: return
Serves as an idiomatic guard clause, exiting the function immediately when value is null.

fields.Front:
[AI Code Audit: Platform Types]
Java method: public String getTitle() { return null; }
Kotlin code:
val title: String = javaObject.getTitle()
What happens at runtime?
fields.Back:
Throws NullPointerException at assignment!

Java methods return "Platform Types" (String!), where Kotlin compiler skips null checks.

Fix: Always declare explicit nullable type on Java interop:
val title: String? = javaObject.getTitle()

fields.Front:
[Kotlin Null Safety]
How does safe casting as? differ from unsafe as?
fields.Back:
as throws ClassCastException if cast fails.

as? returns null on failure instead of crashing:
val number = value as? Int ?: 0

fields.Front:
[Kotlin Collections]
Difference between List<T> and MutableList<T>?
fields.Back:
List<T> is a read-only view (no add(), remove(), clear()).

MutableList<T> provides mutation operations.
In Kotlin standard library, read-only and mutable collection interfaces are strictly segregated.

fields.Front:
[AI Code Audit]
AI writes ViewModel:
class CartViewModel : ViewModel() {
    val items = mutableListOf<CartItem>()
}
Why is this an architectural bug in Android?
fields.Back:
1. Encapsulation leak: UI layer can directly modify items.add(...) bypassing ViewModel validation.
2. Non-reactive: Compose or UI won't observe internal mutations.

Fix: Use private backing property with StateFlow<List<CartItem>>.

fields.Front:
[Kotlin Decision]
When transforming collections in Android, when should you use asSequence()?
fields.Back:
Standard operations (eager): Best for small/medium lists (<1,000 items). Minimal overhead.

asSequence() (lazy): Best for very large lists or long operation chains where you only take the first match (avoids creating intermediate lists in memory).

fields.Front:
[Kotlin Idiom]
What does associateBy do versus groupBy?
fields.Back:
associateBy produces Map<K, V> where each key maps to a single element (duplicates overwrite).

groupBy produces Map<K, List<V>> where each key maps to a list of matching elements.

fields.Front:
[Kotlin Control Flow]
What does it mean that if and when are expressions in Kotlin?
fields.Back:
They return a value! They can be assigned directly to variables or returned from functions:
val status = if (score >= 50) "Pass" else "Fail"
Eliminates temporary mutable accumulator variables.

fields.Front:
[Kotlin Decision]
When to use argument-less when in Kotlin?

[Kotlin Smart Casts]
Why does smart casting work on val but fail on var properties?
fields.Back:
Compiler guarantee: val cannot change after check.

Var property: Another thread or custom getter could mutate the property value between the type check and its usage.

fields.Front:
[AI Code Audit]
AI handles sealed UI state:
when (state) {
    is UiState.Loading -> showSpinner()
    is UiState.Success -> showData(state.data)
    else -> log("unknown")
}
What architectural issue does else create here?
fields.Back:
Defeats compiler exhaustiveness check!

If a developer adds UiState.Error later, compiler won't warn you—it silently falls into else.

Fix: Remove else. Handle every sealed branch explicitly.

fields.Front:
[Kotlin Idiom]
How do Default and Named Arguments in Kotlin eliminate Java's Builder Pattern?
fields.Back:
Default values in function signatures allow callers to pass only required parameters in any order:
fun createButton(text: String, isEnabled: Boolean = true, icon: Icon? = null)
Call: createButton(text = "Save", icon = myIcon)

fields.Front:
[Kotlin Syntax]
What is a single-expression function, and when should it be used?
fields.Back:
Function whose body is a single expression, omitting {} and return:
fun isAdult(age: Int): Boolean = age >= 18
Use for simple transformations, math calculations, or delegating calls.

fields.Front:
[Kotlin Tour: Functions]
What is the trailing lambda convention in Kotlin?
fields.Back:
If the last parameter of a function is a lambda, the curly braces { } can be placed outside the parentheses ( ):
button.setOnClickListener { view -> handleClick() }
This convention is the foundation of Jetpack Compose UI DSLs.

fields.Front:
[AI Code Audit]
AI writes high-frequency utility in Android:
fun <T> measureTime(block: () -> T): T {
    val start = System.currentTimeMillis()
    val res = block()
    Log.d("Perf", "${System.currentTimeMillis() - start}ms")
    return res
}
What optimization keyword should be added and why?
fields.Back:
Add inline:
inline fun <T> measureTime(block: () -> T): T
Reason: Without inline, a new Function object is allocated on heap on every invocation. inline inserts the body directly at call-site.

fields.Front:
[Kotlin Classes]
What 5 methods does a data class automatically generate?
fields.Back:
1. equals() (value equality based on primary constructor properties)
2. hashCode()
3. toString() (e.g. User(name=Alice, age=20))
4. copy() (non-destructive mutation)
5. componentN() (destructuring declarations)

fields.Front:
[Kotlin Decision]
How should you update an existing immutable data class instance in Android state?
fields.Back:
Use the generated .copy() method:
val updatedUser = currentUser.copy(age = currentUser.age + 1)
Produces a fresh instance with specified fields changed while maintaining immutability.

fields.Front:
[Kotlin Architecture]
Why use sealed interface instead of enum class for UI State in Android?
fields.Back:
Enums: Every constant has the exact same properties and no unique data payload.

Sealed interfaces: Each state variant can carry distinct data payload:
sealed interface UiState {
    data object Loading : UiState
    data class Success(val items: List<Item>) : UiState
    data class Error(val error: Throwable) : UiState
}

fields.Front:
[Kotlin Classes]
What is a data object (Kotlin 1.9+)?
fields.Back:
A singleton object that includes generated toString(), equals(), and hashCode().

Ideal for state markers without payloads, such as data object Loading : UiState.

fields.Front:
[AI Code Audit]
AI defines model:
data class Product(val id: String, var price: Double)
Why should properties in a data class be val instead of var?
fields.Back:
Mutating a var in a data class alters its hashCode().

If stored inside a HashSet or HashMap, the object becomes unretrievable or corrupts hash bucket lookups.

fields.Front:
[Kotlin Classes]
What is a companion object in Kotlin?
fields.Back:
An object singleton tied to a class declaration holding factory methods, constants, or helpers.

Unlike Java statics, it is an actual runtime object instance that can implement interfaces.

fields.Front:
[Android Concurrency]
What are the 3 main Kotlin Coroutine Dispatchers and when to use each?
fields.Back:
1. Dispatchers.Main: UI interaction, Compose state updates, small quick callbacks.
2. Dispatchers.IO: Disk reading/writing, database queries (Room), network calls (Retrofit).
3. Dispatchers.Default: CPU-intensive operations (JSON parsing, sorting large datasets).

fields.Front:
[AI Code Audit]
AI writes background fetch in Android:
fun fetchProfile() {
    GlobalScope.launch {
        val profile = api.getProfile()
        updateUi(profile)
    }
}
Identify two fatal bugs in this snippet.
fields.Back:
1. Memory Leak / Uncontrolled Lifecycle: GlobalScope never cancels when Screen closes.
2. Thread crash: updateUi() runs on background thread.

Fix: Use viewModelScope.launch { ... } (scoped to ViewModel lifecycle and runs on Main dispatcher by default).

fields.Front:
[Android Architecture]
When should you use StateFlow versus SharedFlow?
fields.Back:
StateFlow: For persistent UI State (always has initial value, replays latest value to new subscribers).

SharedFlow: For one-time events (snackbars, toast messages, navigation actions) that should not replay on screen rotation.

fields.Front:
[Android Compose]
Why must state inside a Composable function be wrapped in remember { mutableStateOf(...) }?
fields.Back:
Without remember, the state re-initializes to default on every recomposition frame.

remember preserves the state across recompositions inside the composition slot table.

fields.Front:
[AI Code Audit: Jetpack Compose]
AI writes Composable:
@Composable
fun UserProfile(user: User) {
    val formattedDate = SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd").format(user.timestamp)
    Text(text = formattedDate)
}
Why is this a performance footgun in Compose?
fields.Back:
SimpleDateFormat is expensive and gets allocated on every recomposition frame.

Fix: Wrap in remember(user.timestamp) { ... } so it only recomputes when timestamp changes.

fields.Front:
[Kotlin Coroutines]
What does suspend keyword actually do on a function?
fields.Back:
Marks a function that can pause execution without blocking the underlying thread, and resume when result is ready.

Can only be called from inside another suspending function or a coroutine scope.

fields.Front:
[Android Architecture]
What is State Hoisting in Android Jetpack Compose?
fields.Back:
Pattern of moving state upward to make a component stateless, reusable, and easily testable.

A hoisted composable accepts: (value: T, onValueChange: (T) -> Unit) instead of owning internal state.
